clue.text: A complex patricide

explanation.surface: A puzzling case of a son killing his father.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's complex of a boy's desire for his mother is named after the Theban king, who also unknowingly killed his father, a patricide.

clue.text: Ancient home of Sir John (alias Falstaff)

parts.note: ancient means old
an Englishman's home is his castle

explanation.surface: The old seat of Shakespeare's fat knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare first named his comic knight Sir John Oldcastle, renaming him Falstaff after protests from Oldcastle's descendants.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical Lollard knight whose name Shakespeare's character originally bore.

clue.text: Understand Tiny has trouble -standing on it ?

parts.note: to dig is slang for to understand

indicators.note: has trouble suggests the word tiny is in disarray, so its letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A small child struggles to stay on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has trouble' rearranges TINY to NITY. The definition refers to 'standing on one's dignity', insisting on respect.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are pompous are said to stand on their pride and self-respect.

clue.text: Butterfly sleuth

explanation.surface: An investigator chasing a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: Lieutenant Pinkerton is the American officer in Puccini's opera Madama Butterfly; the Pinkerton agency was a famous American detective firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval lover in the opera Madama Butterfly, and a private detective from the Pinkerton agency.

clue.text: Undermines the rising springs

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for springs reads upwards

parts.note: spas are mineral springs

explanation.surface: Rising water from springs eroding foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SPAS to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap is to weaken by digging under, undermining.

clue.text: Mark his successor — Arnold

explanation.surface: A note on who came after Mark, with Arnold named as the heir.
explanation.walkthrough: Scholars hold that Mark's Gospel was written first and the next evangelist drew on it, so he is Mark's successor; Matthew Arnold was the Victorian poet and critic.
explanation.definitionFit: The evangelist whose Gospel followed and used Mark's, and the first name of the poet Arnold, author of Dover Beach.

clue.text: No shellfish served up with wine? He's annoyed

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means the words no and shellfish read upwards

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish
tent is a dark red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A diner served no shellfish, only wine, is cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns NOCLAM to MALCON.
explanation.definitionFit: A malcontent is a dissatisfied, discontented person.

clue.text: Frightened to put up request for reduction of light?

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the phrase for the request reads upwards

parts.note: dim it is an order to lower the light

explanation.surface: Too scared to ask for the lights to be lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns DIM IT to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Timid means shy and easily frightened.

clue.text: Arrange the race area

indicators.note: arrange means the letters of the words the race are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Organising the race venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' rearranges THERACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric unit of land area, ten thousand square metres.

clue.text: No beer then in the East and North of the country ?

definitions.text: No beer then in the East and North of the country ?

parts.words: No beer then in the East and North of the country ?
parts.note: the west of Britain, by contrast with the east and north, recalls the old law shutting its pubs on Sundays

explanation.surface: A drinker finds no beer on offer in one part of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Under the Welsh Sunday Closing Act of 1881 the principality's pubs stayed shut on Sundays; the country lies west of England, not east or north.
explanation.definitionFit: The country in western Britain where for decades no alcohol was sold on Sundays.

clue.text: No tribe turned to the Philistine god

indicators.note: turned means the two words no and tribe, once replaced, are read right to left

parts.note: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: A tribe that has abandoned its own faith for a Philistine idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses NOGAD as a whole, giving DAG + ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The half-fish deity worshipped by the Philistines, whose temple Samson brought down.

clue.text: Controversial European claim perhaps

parts.note: a Pole is a European, from Poland

indicators.note: perhaps tells the solver the letters of claim are only one possible arrangement

explanation.surface: A disputed assertion made by someone from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CLAIM to MICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something polemical is argumentative, stirring up dispute.

clue.text: It's like one of the French sayings on stage

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
I is the Roman numeral for one
des is French for 'of the' (plural)

explanation.surface: A comparison with French theatrical remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks spoken by an actor to the audience, unheard by other characters on stage.

clue.text: Blimey-faces the last of the drinks!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey
dials are clock faces or faces in slang

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims as faces turn to the final round.
explanation.walkthrough: COR and 'blimey' are both Cockney-flavoured British exclamations of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet liqueurs were traditionally served at the end of a meal, after the wine.

clue.text: Marine gasteropod flower

explanation.surface: A sea snail named after a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible sea snail called a winkle, and the blue-flowered trailing plant Vinca.

clue.text: Have a go with Simon Templar by appointment

parts.note: to have a go is to try
Simon Templar is the Saint, the fictional hero; ST abbreviates saint

explanation.surface: Trying one's luck with the famous fictional adventurer at a fixed meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon Templar is Leslie Charteris's crime-fighter known as the Saint, so he gives ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a prearranged meeting, especially between lovers.

clue.text: Roughly ten metres, taken between courses

indicators.note: roughly suggests ten metres are given only approximately, here meaning their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A measurement of about ten metres separating racecourses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' anagrams TENMETRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A French term for a light dish or sweet served between the main courses of a meal.

clue.text: Suet mixed with heavenly butter causes watery mouths

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of suet are stirred together

parts.note: Aries is the Ram, a constellation in the sky, and rams butt

explanation.surface: Suet blended with a divine spread makes mouths water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges SUET to ESTU. 'Butter' is one that butts, not the dairy spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Estuaries are the tidal mouths of rivers.

clue.text: A mineral for a sailor-boy, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase for sailor-boy is spoken, matching the answer's sound

parts.note: a salt is a sailor and Peter is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A mineral suited to a young seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre is potassium nitrate, a natural mineral used in gunpowder.

clue.text: More drinking time for a telephone eavesdropper ?

explanation.surface: Wanting a later closing time to listen in on calls.
explanation.walkthrough: British pubs had strict licensing hours, and an extension allowed drinking later; a second handset on the same line lets someone listen in.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence permitting longer opening hours, and an additional phone on a line through which one can overhear.

clue.text: The Palace — best part of the trip, soon to end

indicators.note: to end places the word for soon at the finish
the best part means most of the word, all but its last letter

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: The palace was the highlight of the tour, which is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best part of' drops the last letter of TRIP to leave TRI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand and Petit Trianon are palaces in the grounds of Versailles.

clue.text: Many in queue for tongue

indicators.note: in places the letter for many within the word for queue

parts.note: a tail is a line of people, a queue
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Lots of people waiting in line for a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a Dravidian language of southern India and Sri Lanka; tongue means language.

clue.text: Warlike poet

explanation.surface: A belligerent versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial means fit for war, and Martial was the Roman poet famed for his epigrams.

clue.text: A winding stair and so to our geology period

indicators.note: a winding staircase twists, so the letters of the word stair are twisted round

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: Climbing a spiral staircase and so arriving at a geological era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges STAIR to TRIAS; 'A' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Triassic is the first period of the Mesozoic era, a division of geological time.

clue.text: Chinese secret societies make sugar-grab

explanation.surface: Chinese gangs snatching sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: Tongs were Chinese secret brotherhoods, often criminal; sugar tongs pick up sugar lumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongs are both Chinese criminal brotherhoods and a hinged tool for picking up sugar lumps.

clue.text: Cause of trouble in a boat

indicators.note: the letters of cause are in trouble, so they are disordered

explanation.surface: Something causing problems aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of trouble' rearranges CAUSE. The boat is a sauce boat, the jug that carries gravy to the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravy or sauce is served from a boat-shaped jug.

clue.text: Minor weekend blow for the governor

parts.note: Sat, a shortened (minor) form of Saturday, is a weekend day
a rap is a sharp blow

explanation.surface: A small knock at the end of the week for the man in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia.

clue.text: Share speculator closes Bonn's lower house

indicators.note: the closing letters of the parliament's name are kept, its opening dropped

parts.note: the Bundestag was West Germany's lower parliament, which sat in Bonn

explanation.surface: A speculator shuts down the German parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closes' keeps the end of BUNDESTAG, dropping BUNDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag buys new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit.

clue.text: Ann disturbed by trumpet sound in Massachusetts

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of Ann are stirred into a new order

parts.note: a tucket is an old word for a flourish on a trumpet, as in Shakespeare's stage directions

explanation.surface: A woman named Ann is woken by a trumpet blast in New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' gives NAN from ANN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantucket is an island off Cape Cod in the state of Massachusetts.

clue.text: Whose blinking portrait in the silver casket ?

definitions.text: Whose blinking portrait in the silver casket ?

parts.words: Whose blinking portrait in the silver casket ?
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice, Arragon opens the silver casket and finds 'the portrait of a blinking' fool, and 'blinking' also reads as a mild British curse

explanation.surface: A question about whose face appears in Portia's silver casket.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, Portia's suitors choose among gold, silver and lead caskets; the Prince of Arragon picks silver and finds 'the portrait of a blinking idiot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line names a fool in the casket, and blinking is a British euphemistic curse word.

clue.text: Frank the engineer follows after

indicators.note: follows places the letters for the engineer after the word for after

parts.note: since means after, from a past time
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A man named Frank comes after the engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and sincere both mean honest and open.

clue.text: Ballerina's part is grand-is she French ?

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: Is that grand dancer a Frenchwoman?
explanation.definitionFit: The title role of Adam's romantic ballet is one of the great parts for a ballerina.
